title: nD grammar descriptor
description: What an nD grammar (a 'plane') publishes to attach to 5D (spec/SPEC.md §9). This $id resolves once the repository is published; until then, resolve schema $refs from a local copy (see tests/test_conformance.py's _local_validator()). The JSON INTERCHANGE form (produce omitted — JSON cannot carry a callable) validates directly against this schema. The RUNTIME form additionally requires 'produce' to be present and callable, which a JSON Schema cannot express structurally — see src/five_d_nd/contract.py descriptor_violations(require_produce=True) for that half of the contract. Ported from versum src/versum/planes.py's DescriptorPlane.from_descriptor — a binding value is a BARE DIMENSION STRING, exactly matching versum's own p5.is_dimension(dim) check (5D is neutral on is/ought, §7 N1; owner design change, 2026-10-01 — supersedes an earlier mode-aware object form on this branch, see docs/decisions/0003-is-ought-in-nd-grammars.md). This specification's own additions beyond versum's own contract: the required contract_version conformance marker (§9/§10, MUST equal the spec version exactly); the optional co_dimensions list (§9 N3, each id MUST be a declared NDSystem axis); an optional, UNCHECKED context value on each example (§9, for a context-dependent grammar such as topos — versum parity: a non-mapping context, e.g. a string or null, is accepted).

contract_version.description: Conformance marker (§9/§10): MUST equal, exactly, the 5D spec version this descriptor targets — 'How a grammar declares conformance' in §9. For this draft, that value is '1.0-draft' (src/five_d_nd/contract.py SPEC_VERSION). Not part of versum's own descriptor contract.

co_dimensions.description: OPTIONAL (§9 N3 — the owner's settled rule: a grammar MAY, never MUST, mark the normative character of a relation this way). A list of axis ids FROM THIS DESCRIPTOR'S OWN nd_system.axes — each one a co-dimension the grammar is declaring. Validated only for cross-reference (each id names a declared axis); absent entirely is valid (see conformance/vectors/descriptor-binding/).

allOf.description: unknown_values: 'reject' is checked HERE, at the descriptor layer — matching versum, where this is a planes.py check, not an NDSystem.violations() check (see nd-system.schema.json's own description). This nd_system value MAY itself be wrapper-form ({"nd_system": {...}}, see nd-system.schema.json); versum's own descriptor-layer check reads validation.unknown_values off the SAME (unwrapped) level its NDSystem.from_dict uses. An earlier version of this allOf branch constrained the OUTER object's own 'validation' unconditionally, which is the WRONG level whenever nd_system is wrapper-form — an outer-level validation.unknown_values is not what versum or src/five_d_nd/contract.py descriptor_violations() actually read in that shape. This if/then/else mirrors nd-system.schema.json's own unwrap-first branching exactly, applied to 'validation' alone. 'validation' itself MAY be any JSON-falsy value (null, 0, false, "", []), not only an object — versum's own `validation = root.get("validation") or {}` accepts every falsy shape (equivalent to {}, so unknown_values defaults to "reject") and CRASHES only on a TRUTHY non-mapping; this mirrors that exactly, same as nd-system.schema.json's own 'validation' field.

binding.description: relation_or_field -> one of the five dimensions (a bare string; versum's own shape — p5.is_dimension(dim)). 5D does not inspect whether a relation is normative (§7 N1-N2): a normative relation binds exactly like any other. Whether a relation IS normative is the owning nD grammar's own knowledge, carried as a co-dimension on that grammar's own NDSystem (§9 N3) — never expressed here.

produce.description: REQUIRED and callable in the runtime descriptor form; OMITTED in the JSON interchange form (§9). Not itself JSON-Schema-checkable for callability.

context.description: OPTIONAL (§9). Passed through UNCHECKED to produce(sentence, context) when present — a context-dependent grammar (e.g. topos) needs this to reproduce its own examples. No type constraint here, by versum parity: versum accepts a non-mapping context (a bare string, null, ...) and never validates its shape.
